text: M11 `m11pjres` says path matching and the id lookup (also in the `--project` branch) go over the views of both kinds and that an unreadable `workspace.json` is WORKSPACE_FILE_INVALID, but not WHEN a broken file of one registered home refuses a resolution that may not need it. Assumed: the refusal applies exactly where the answer depends on that file. Walk-up: when the project directory (or, without a marker, the cwd) lies inside the broken home — unless `--workspace` names a workspace that does hold the project. `--project <id>`: when the broken workspace is among the candidates (all workspaces without `--workspace`, or the named one), even if another workspace has the id, because the broken file could list it too and the 0/1/N count cannot be told (no guessing); the hint offers `--workspace <name>`. A home whose directory no longer exists (`home-missing`) is not a file to repair: it reads as a workspace with no projects and never refuses. On the `cli` path this replaces the PROJECT_* miss with an `unreadable:` suffix of dev-0103; the `mcp`/`internal` path (no WORKSPACE_* codes there per the `ask` record) keeps PROJECT_ID_NOT_FOUND with that suffix. All WorkspaceFileError codes of the file (also _PROJECT_ID_MISSING / _DUPLICATE) surface as WORKSPACE_FILE_INVALID, the original code inside the message.
assumption: ASSUMPTION:dev-0402 — a broken workspace.json refuses a cli resolution only where the answer depends on it (dir inside that home; that workspace among the --project candidates); a missing home never refuses.
